result.topic_en: End of a fragment giving numerical examples of numbers pq(pp-qq) and xy(xx-yy) with equal products, then fragment 70 (Krafft) on making x+y+z a square with xyz=1, and the start of fragment 71 (Lexell) on choosing N so that aa+Mbb and aa+Nbb are both squares.
result.transcription:
Ita sumto $s=1$ et $t=1$ pro casu $n=2$ erit $p=71$, $q=85$, $x=71$, $y=20$. Hic loco $p$ et $q$ eorum semisumma et semidifferentia sumi possunt fietque $p=2.3.13$ et $q=7$. Hinc enim fiet
$pq(pp-qq)=2.3.5.7.13.17.71$ et $xy(xx-yy)=3.5.7.13.17.71$.
Sin autem sumatur $n=-2$ manente $s=t=1$, prodit $p=9$, $q=5.9$, sive $p=1$ et $q=5$, sive etiam $p=3$ et $q=2$, tum vero erit $x=9$, $y=4.9$, sive $x=1$ et $y=4$, tum enim erit
$pq(pp-qq)=2.3.5$ et $xy(xx-yy)=3.5$.
A. m. T. III. p. 121-123.

b) Quaestiones ad resolutionem plurium aequationum ducentes.

70.
(W. L. Krafft.)

Problema. Efficere, ut fiat $x+y+z=\square$ et $xyz=1$, ideoque $z=\frac{1}{xy}$.
Sequentes solutiones particulares prodierunt
I. $x=\frac{1}{2}$, $y=\frac{9}{2}$, $z=\frac{4}{9}$
II. $x=\frac{2}{9}$, $y=\frac{50}{9}$, $z=\frac{81}{100}$
III. $x=\frac{13}{392}$, $y=\frac{117}{392}$, $z=\frac{392^2}{9.13^2}$
IV. $x=\frac{2}{5}$, $y=\frac{18}{5}$, $z=\frac{25}{36}$
V. $x=-2$, $y=-\frac{2}{9}$, $z=\frac{9}{4}$
VI. $x=\frac{1}{6}$, $y=\frac{1}{12}$, $z=72$.
Si ratio $x$ ad $y$ sumatur $a:b$, et ponatur $x=ma$ et $y=mb$, erit $z=\frac{1}{mmab}$, unde fieri debet
$m(a+b)+\frac{1}{mmab}=\square$, sive $m^3(a+b)+\frac{1}{ab}=\square$,
seu $m^3aabb(a+b)+ab=\square$.
A. m. T. I. p. 121.

71.
(Lexell.)
Ut formulae $aa+Mbb$ et $aa+Nbb$ quadrata reddi queant, posito $M=m\mu$ capiatur $N=(app+m)(aqq+\mu)$, sicque pro dato numero $M$ infiniti valores idonei pro $N$ reperiuntur, veluti si $M=1$, ideoque $m=\mu=\pm1$, erit $N=(app\pm1)(aqq\pm1)$. Si $p=1$, erit $N=(a\pm1)(aqq\pm1)$, cujusmodi formulae sunt
pro $a=1$, $N=2(qq+1)$
$a=2$, $N=3(2qq+1)$, $2qq-1$
$a=3$, $N=4(3qq+1)$, $2(3qq-1)$
$a=4$, $N=5(4qq+1)$, $3(4qq-1)$.

methods.what: Numerical examples where pq(pp-qq) and xy(xx-yy) differ by a factor 2 (taking p,q as half-sum and half-difference)
Small example of the same relation
Particular rational solutions of x+y+z square with xyz=1
Reduction via x=ma, y=mb to a single square condition in m
Construction of N such that aa+Mbb and aa+Nbb can both be squares, given M=mμ
Special case M=1 giving families of N

items.quote: Problema. Efficere, ut fiat $x+y+z=\square$ et $xyz=1$, ideoque $z=\frac{1}{xy}$.
items.english: Problem. To bring it about that x+y+z is a square and xyz=1, and hence z=1/(xy).

items.quote: Ut formulae $aa+Mbb$ et $aa+Nbb$ quadrata reddi queant, posito $M=m\mu$ capiatur $N=(app+m)(aqq+\mu)$, sicque pro dato numero $M$ infiniti valores idonei pro $N$ reperiuntur
items.english: So that the formulas aa+Mbb and aa+Nbb can be made squares, putting M=mμ, take N=(app+m)(aqq+μ); thus for a given number M infinitely many suitable values of N are found.
